Article Title: How a 37-year-old Von Miller with 138.5 career sacks plans to haunt quarterbacks one more time? This time for America's Team
Article Text:
Von Miller signs with Cowboys (Getty Images)

Can Von Miller still get to the quarterback at 37?

What does Von Miller's signing mean for the Cowboys' pass rush in 2026?

Why did Von Miller choose the Dallas Cowboys over other teams?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Von Miller spent weeks working out near The Star in Frisco, posting photoshopped images of himself in a Cowboys uniform and dropping hints that Dallas was where he wanted to be. On Sunday night, it became official. The 37-year-old pass rusher, who leads all active NFL players with 138.5 career sacks, agreed to a one-year deal with the Dallas Cowboys, completing a homecoming years in the making. Miller grew up in DeSoto, Texas, just 30 minutes from AT&T Stadium, and attended Texas A&M before becoming one of the most feared edge rushers in NFL history.The short answer is yes. And last season gave every reason to believe it.With the Washington Commanders in 2025, Von Miller posted nine sacks across 17 games while starting just three and playing only 37 percent of the defensive snaps. Nine sacks from 420 snaps. That production rate would turn heads from a player half his age. For Miller at 36, it was a reminder that his instincts and technique still work when his body is fresh. He is no longer an every-down defender, and the Cowboys are not expecting him to be one. But as a situational pass rusher who picks his spots, he still has the tools to make quarterbacks uncomfortable.The numbers behind his career tell a bigger story. Miller's 138.5 sacks put him tied with Hall of Famer and former Cowboy DeMarcus Ware for ninth in NFL history.Just four more sacks in Dallas would move him past Terrell Suggs, Jason Taylor, and Michael Strahan into sixth all-time. At his snap rate from last season, that milestone is well within reach. In the playoffs, he has 10.5 sacks across 16 career games, the most among any active player. The big moments have never intimidated him.Miller confirmed the news Sunday night on social media, posting a picture of himself in a Cowboys uniform with the caption: "Dallas! Let's make this one Special."Dallas already had one of the more intriguing edge units heading into the season. Rashan Gary, acquired in a trade from Green Bay, brings athleticism and proven production. Donovan Ezeiruaku, a second-round pick in 2025, showed flashes of something real in his rookie year. First-round rookie Malachi Lawrence is a player this coaching staff believes in. Now they get Miller too.Defensive coordinator Christian Parker, who briefly overlapped with Miller in Denver in 2021, knows what this signing is and is not. It is not a plug-and-play starter. It is a chess piece. Parker spoke about his young linebacker group at training camp in June with genuine confidence: "It's a younger group, but it's a hungry group. I think we're going to have the play style that we want. Those guys want to be held accountable. They want to be responsible for stopping the run and affecting the quarterback, and we'll be able to do that."Adding Miller to that room does not crowd those younger players out. If anything, it accelerates their development. Having a two-time Super Bowl champion, an eight-time Pro Bowl selection, and the active sack leader showing up every day is not a roadblock for Ezeiruaku or Lawrence. It is a masterclass. The Cowboys are not just signing a rotational pass rusher. They are putting a future Hall of Famer in a mentorship role with their most important young defenders.This was not purely a business decision. Von Miller had options. He enters his 15th season as one of the most decorated pass rushers in the game, and teams around the league were aware of what he showed in Washington. But from the moment he started training near The Star this summer, the message was clear: he wanted to come home.Miller's path to Dallas was not a straight line. He won his first Super Bowl with the Broncos in 2016, earning MVP honors. A half-season stint with the Rams brought a second ring in 2022. Then came three seasons with the Buffalo Bills, interrupted by a torn ACL that cost him significant time in 2022 and 2023. Washington gave him a fresh start in 2025, and he delivered. Now, after five teams and 14 seasons, he gets to play professional football in the state where he grew up, for the team his region has always followed.The Cowboys open their 2026 season against the New York Giants on Sunday Night Football. It is a stage Miller has performed on many times before. For Dallas, a team carrying real playoff ambitions this year, having a proven pass rusher who can win in key moments is exactly the kind of low-risk, high-upside addition that smart rosters are built on. The price is modest. The potential return is not.
Article Summary: Von miller signs a one-year deal with the dallas cowboys. The 37-year-old pass rusher leads all active nfl players with 138.5 career sacks. Miller grew up in desoto, texas, just 30 minutes from at&t stadium. The cowboys open their 2026 season against the new york giants on sunday night football.

Article Title: Luka Doncic vs. Thanos? 6-foot-2 Sixers guard makes surprising pick for Marvel showdown

Doncic's numbers back up the confidence

Tyrese Maxey says Luka Doncic is the only NBA player he would trust to beat Thanos one-on-one. The Philadelphia 76ers guard made the pick during a recent interview with Complex, choosing the Los Angeles Lakers star over everyone else in the league.Doncic enters the 2026-27 season as the unquestioned face of the Lakers after LeBron James's move to Philadelphia, and Maxey's pick lands right as the two players' teams sit on opposite ends of that trade. It's a lighthearted aside, but it says something about how rivals view Doncic's competitive streak.Maxey was asked which player could beat Thanos one-on-one, and he named Doncic without hesitating. He pointed to Doncic's mentality as the reason, saying, "Luka just ain't scared of nothing, you know what I mean?" Maxey added that he could picture Doncic squaring up against the villain on an island somewhere, using his signature stepback to shake a defender several feet taller than him. “I can see Luka on an island, 1v1ing Thanos…I think Luka can step back pretty much anybody. I don’t think Thanos would scare him at all.”He doesn't think Thanos, who stands roughly 8-foot-3 in Marvel lore, would rattle Doncic at all. The big bad who scared almost every Avengers superhero, including Iron Man, Thor, Spider-Man, Ant-Man and pthers would not scare Purple and Gold's superstar.The praise tracks with what Doncic has actually done on an NBA floor.He posted 33.5 points, 7.7 rebounds and 8.3 assists last season on 47.6 percent shooting from the field and 36.6 percent from three. His best all-around year came in 2023-24, when he averaged 33.9 points, 9.2 rebounds and 9.8 assists.At 27, Doncic is producing at a level that keeps him in the MVP conversation every year he stays healthy, which makes Maxey's confidence in him easier to understand.Doncic's offseason hasn't been limited to comic-book hypotheticals. The Lakers were sold again this summer, with Mark Walter agreeing to hand his majority stake to Bob Iger and Joshua Kushner in a deal valued at $12.5 billion, just a year after Walter had taken control. General manager Rob Pelinka has spent the offseason building a roster around Doncic regardless of who signs the checks upstairs. Doncic wasn't consulted on the sale, but he said he's ready to start building a relationship with Iger and Kushner once the season gets underway.Doncic will have to introduce himself to his new owners at some point this year, a conversation that carries more weight than a hypothetical matchup with a comic-book villain. But if Maxey's read on him holds up, neither one should rattle him.

Travis Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs’ popular tight end, recorded 76 receptions for 851 yards and 5 touchdowns across all 17 games in the last season. Ahead of the new season, Travis Kelce’s comments have resurfaced showing how focused he is on his performance.Last year, after losing in Super Bowl LX against the Philadelphia Eagles, Travis Kelce opened up about it on his podcast, New Heights, as he said, “I’m kicking myself for some of the tiny, tiny decisions I made on the field…I wasn’t the best leader that I could be in motivating my guys and keeping my guys calm, cool and collected.”The former Super Bowl champion added, “I put a lot of that on myself as the guy that’s been in the building for 12 years and seen a lot of football and actually seen a situation just like this in the Super Bowl,” Travis Kelce said. “It’s a tough pill to swallow. It’s a hard reality, man.”The popular tight end continued, “I’m sorry for how it ended..I have a beautiful life, man. I have loved ones, I have the most amazing family in the world that supports me in everything that I do and they were all there cheering me on and hoping for the best on Sunday, man.”Over the last few years, Travis Kelce has attracted a lot of criticism about his performance as many are curious about why he has not announced his retirement yet.With all the buzz around his personal life, many have felt that the Kansas City Chiefs’ popular tight end has remained distracted on the field.To make matters worse, just weeks ahead of the new season, there have been concerns about Travis Kelce’s overall fitness as many feel he has become out of shape during the offseason.In an interview with A to Z Sports' Charles Goldman, the Kansas City Chiefs' head coach Andy Reid has defended Travis Kelce and recently added, "He's great for the young guys. Article Title: Inspiring story on motherhood: “Once I had my first child, I didn’t want to leave his side”- How Chris Evert found a deeper kind of happiness after becoming a mother
Article Text:

Why Chris Evert did not want to leave her first child’s side

Why Chris Evert’s words still matter years later

We Are Tennis

For Chris Evert, becoming a mother changed what she wanted from life. The tennis great had already walked away from professional tennis when she welcomed her first son, Alexander James, in 1991. But motherhood gave her a feeling that went far beyond retirement. Evert has said, “Once I had my first child, I didn’t want to leave his side.” The simple line explains why her first child quickly became more important than the sport that had defined her for years.Evert became a mother on October 12, 1991, when she and her then husband, former Olympic skier Andy Mill, welcomed Alexander James Mill. She was 36 at the time and had retired from professional tennis two years earlier.Even though Evert was no longer playing full time, tennis had not completely disappeared from her life. She had worked in broadcasting after retirement and had considered taking part in team tennis and exhibition matches. Then Alexander was born, and her plans changed.In a 1992 interview with the, Evert spoke openly about the effect her baby had on her. She said she had thought about returning to the sport while she was pregnant.But after holding Alexander in the hospital, those thoughts disappeared.“I held the baby in the hospital and after the first minute, all those feelings were gone,” Evert said.That helps explain the meaning behind her later comment about not wanting to leave his side. She had spent most of her life preparing for matches, traveling for tournaments and dealing with the pressure that came with being one of the best players in the world. Now, she had a baby who depended on her, and being there with him felt more important.The change was not about suddenly disliking tennis. Evert had simply found something that meant more to her at that stage of her life.Alexander was not just Evert’s first child. His arrival gave her a new way to measure what mattered.Before becoming a mother, much of Evert’s public life centered on tennis. She won 18 Grand Slam singles titles and spent years near the top of the sport. Winning was a huge part of her identity. Motherhood gave her a role where there was no ranking, trophy or scoreboard.Thereported in 1991 that Evert compared winning Wimbledon with having a baby. Her view was striking. A major title could bring happiness and recognition, but the feeling did not last in the same way. Having her child was something she could hold on to.“The great high of winning Wimbledon lasts for about a week,” Evert told, according to the. “But having a baby, there just isn’t any comparison.”Her words show why the birth of Alexander was such a turning point. Evert had already achieved the biggest goals in tennis. She did not need another trophy to prove what she could do. Instead, she wanted to enjoy the new part of her life that had arrived.That did not mean she stopped being Chris Evert the tennis champion. It meant she had become Chris Evert the mother too, and she was learning that the second role could bring a different kind of happiness.Alexander was the first of Evert and Andy Mill’s three sons. Nicholas was born in 1994, followed by Colton in 1996. Together, the boys became the center of a busy family life.Evert later made it clear that her feelings about motherhood had not faded as her children grew. In a 2001 interview with the, she spoke about Alexander, Nicholas and Colton while they were still young.“They’re my life, they’re the most important thing,” Evert said. “I’m busy, but I’m 100 percent a mom first.”That comment adds another layer to her earlier quote. Evert was not talking only about the excitement of having her first baby. She was describing a lasting change in how she saw herself.Her sons also grew up around sports because both of their parents were successful athletes. Still, Evert did not push them to follow the same path she had taken. She wanted them to enjoy being children instead of feeling that they had to become champions.In a later interview with, Evert again placed motherhood above her tennis achievements. Asked about the best part of being Chris Evert, she immediately pointed to her sons and being a mother.“I love my boys,” she said. “That’s been the highlight of my life.”That answer is important because it came decades after Alexander was born. Her feelings were not limited to those first few months of motherhood. They remained part of how Evert viewed her life long after her playing career had ended.Evert’s quote is simple, but it says something many parents can understand. Having a child can change what feels urgent. Things that once seemed extremely important can suddenly move down the list.For Evert, that shift came after years of living with the demands of professional tennis. She had known what it meant to spend months traveling and competing. She had also known the feeling of winning major titles in front of huge crowds.Yet when Alexander arrived, she wanted to stay close to him.That decision did not erase tennis from her life. Evert later worked as a coach, mentor and commentator, and she remained connected to the sport she had helped shape. But her relationship with tennis was different because she no longer needed to prove herself through competition.Her three sons became the part of her life she spoke about with the most pride. In 2025,again asked her about the best thing about being Chris Evert. Her answer centered on being a mother.That is why the line, “Once I had my first child, I didn’t want to leave his side,” carries more meaning than it may seem to at first. Evert was not simply describing a mother wanting to stay with her newborn. She was describing the moment her priorities changed.For a woman who had spent decades being defined by tennis, motherhood became the part of her identity she valued most. And for Evert, that change began with one child, Alexander, and the feeling that nothing else mattered quite as much as being beside him.

Antonio Felix da Costa secured a podium at the London E-Prix on Saturday but was still slightly disappointed after falling short of keeping his Formula E title hopes alive this season. The Jaguar TCS Racing driver is now fifth in the Drivers’ Standings after finishing third in the Round 16 race and is focusing on helping the team secure its second Teams’ Championship.Antonio Felix da Costa started seventh on the grid and managed to make some important overtakes to clinch third place on the podium.Sharing his feelings after the Round 16 race, Da Costa said, “It is a bittersweet feeling – it is always good to be on the podium and I was able to make some overtakes to make progress in the race. Unfortunately, the FCY totally scuppered Mitch’s race, so we were unable to maximise our full pace and the result for the team at home. It is a tough one and I feel for him, but we just have to attack the final race in a positive frame of mind, make sure we qualify strongly and get it over the line tomorrow. ”ID@undefinedCaption not available.Talking about how Porsche drivers Pascal Wehrlein and Nico Muller dominated from the front row of the grid, he said, “We saw the games that Porsche was playing, but they had the track position to do that.It’s not necessarily what we want to see, and I’ve heard it before from other people that those were dirty games, but they played them – fair enough. Article Title: Michael Sam coming out story: “We were so secretive. He was out and I was in the closet” - How the first openly gay NFL player overcame a troubled childhood to make football history
Article Text:
Michael Sam coming out story: “We were so secretive. He was out and I was in the closet” — How the first openly gay NFL draftee overcame a troubled childhood to make football history (Image via Getty: Michael Sam​)

Michael Sam’s troubled childhood story

Michael Sam’s mother was unsupportive but his father encouraged him to play football

Michael Sam knew in high school that he was attracted to men

Michael Sam was pushed by Vito Cammisano to confront his identity

Michael Sam came out to his Missouri Tigers teammates before his senior season

Michael Sam’s NFL journey continued with the Dallas Cowboys

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Michael Sam came out publicly as gay in February 2014 through an interview with The New York Times. At the time, he was a defensive lineman for the Missouri Tigers at the University of Missouri.When he began the interview, Sam said: “I’m Michael Sam. I’m a football player, and I’m gay. Is this a huge deal? I understand it is, but my purpose and focus right now is playing football.”He had already told his teammates about his sexual orientation several months earlier, before entering the 2014 NFL Draft. By coming out publicly, Sam was poised to become the first openly gay player selected by an NFL team.Sam did not want his sexuality to overshadow his biggest ambition: succeeding on the football field and earning an opportunity to play in the NFL.Football had been an important outlet and a powerful source of strength for him throughout his troubled childhood.Michael Sam’s parents, JoAnn Sam and Michael Sam Sr., had eight children. Before Sam was born, the family lost his sister, Chanel, under tragic circumstances. Later, they lost his older brother, Russell, who was shot after trespassing on private land.When Sam was five, his father left the family. His mother worked, while his older brother Julian took care of Sam and his siblings for the next three years.But in 1998, Julian disappeared after leaving Sam and his little sister at the school bus stop.“Julian went missing in October, 1998. It was on a Friday when the last time me and little sister saw him. In the mornings, Julian used to always wait by me and little sister for the bus.As the bus came close, he went to the back of the house and waved at us; we waved back, and we never saw him again. It was like he vanished,” Sam said via Hollywood Medium with Tyler Henry in February 2026.The tragedies did not stop there. Sam experienced abuse from two older brothers who were involved with gangs and drugs, and had to take on childcare responsibilities.Only two things provided him with an escape: school and football.Michael Sam’s mother, JoAnn Sam, was not supportive of his involvement in sports, but his estranged father, Michael Sam Sr., returned and encouraged him to play football.Sam has remembered his father’s support in convincing his mother to let him play as one of the few positive things his father did for him.According to Oprah.com, Sam grew up as a self-described “mama’s boy” in the small town of Hitchcock, Texas.Sports eventually became his outlet. “Becoming a teenager, I needed sports,” Sam told Oprah in December 2014. “I knew I wanted to make something of myself. I knew sports taught me, and my coaches taught me, the discipline that I have today. I needed it.”Sam was so talented that he made the varsity team as a freshman, a rare achievement in football-crazy Texas. At the time, he did not dream of playing college football. He thought he would work in the oil refineries of nearby Texas City after high school.But his talent attracted college football coaches’ attention, and recruitment letters began arriving. Sam wanted to play Division I football, which meant he also needed to perform well academically.After four attempts, and just days before his recruitment deadline, he cleared the required SAT threshold. Scholarship offers followed, and after considering his options, he eventually chose the University of Missouri.It was during high school that Michael Sam realized he was attracted to men.“In the summer of 2009, I had experimentation, and sure enough afterward I knew I was pretty damn gay; that’s when I knew,” Sam said via Worcester State University’s Diversity Lecture Series in September 2017.“So, I became a freshman at the University of Missouri knowing that I am gay, but I still tried to deny it. I said to myself, ‘Well, what do I do? Do I come out? Is this just a phase? What is this?’”Sam tried to bury his feelings during college, but they eventually resurfaced - especially after he met University of Missouri swimmer Vito Cammisano.“He pretty much changed my life forever. We hit it off fast. We started dating secretly. It was like a fairy tale. I was so happy. I’d never been so happy in my life,” Sam said.The college romance eventually became complicated as rumors about Michael Sam and Vito Cammisano’s relationship began circulating. Sam was still in the closet, while Cammisano was already openly gay.“I didn’t take that well because I’m a football player and I’m a big guy and I’m not supposed to be gay and this isn’t supposed to be happening. So, I started distancing myself from Vito, and I was not in a good place,” Sam said.“We were so secretive,” Sam said. “After so many fights, Vito had kind of had enough. He was tired of this lifestyle because he was out and I was in the closet.”After one argument, Vito asked Sam who he saw when he looked in the mirror. The question affected Sam deeply because he did not know the answer.“I was a pretender trying to be someone I’m not,” he said.Sam began exploring the LGBTQ community to better understand himself. He participated in St. Louis Pride, where he found that nobody judged him or treated him differently. Instead, he encountered people who were welcoming and accepting.He later became involved with the LGBTQ community in Columbia, Missouri, and experienced the same sense of warmth and acceptance.Then came the biggest challenge: opening up to his teammates.During the training camp in August 2013, before his senior season, Michael Sam decided to tell his Missouri teammates that he was gay. He was nervous about how they would react, but their response truly surprised him.His teammates rallied around him and supported him. They were happy that he had finally opened up and treated him like one of their own.That experience changed Sam’s outlook. If his teammates could accept him, he believed other football teams could too.“I came out to my team this last August, and coming out to them, they rallied around me, they supported me,” Sam later said. “And I knew in that moment that this can happen anywhere; if my team can support me, any team can support me.”Missouri finished the 2013 season with a 12-2 record, while Sam established himself as one of the best defensive players in college football. He won SEC Defensive Player of the Year and entered the NFL Draft as one of the most prominent prospects at the time.In February 2014, Sam made his sexuality public. Three months later, the St. Louis Rams selected him with the 249th overall pick in the seventh round of the 2014 NFL Draft, making him the first openly gay player drafted by an NFL team.Michael Sam did not make the St. Louis Rams’ final 53-man roster. He was subsequently claimed by no team on waivers and joined the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad in September 2014.The Cowboys waived him from their practice squad in October 2014 to make space for linebacker Troy Davis. He never appeared in a regular-season NFL game.In 2015, Sam participated in the NFL’s first Veteran Combine, where he ran the 40-yard dash in 4.99 seconds. Later that year, he signed a two-year contract with the CFL’s Montreal Alouettes.Sam became the first openly gay player to play in a CFL regular-season game when he appeared for Montreal in August 2015. He ultimately played one regular-season game for the Alouettes.After stepping away from professional football, Sam eventually returned to the sport as a coach. He played for the Barcelona Dragons in the European League of Football in 2022 before moving into coaching.In 2026, Sam joined the Berlin Thunder coaching staff as the team’s linebacker coach, continuing his football journey from historical NFL prospect to coach.

Novak Djokovic has revealed that a health problem he has dealt with for years played a part in his Cincinnati Open loss to Thiago Agustín Tirante. The 39-year-old looked unwell during the match on Saturday, August 15, falling to his hands and knees and appearing to vomit into a towel. Djokovic said heat and humidity can make the condition harder to handle, while stressing weather itself was not main problem.Djokovic started the match strongly against Tirante, taking the first set 6-2. Things changed in the second set, however, as the Serbian began struggling physically. He went down on his hands and knees and called for a medical timeout.He then sat on the bench while a doctor and physiotherapist attended to him. Djokovic removed his shirt and used an ice pack on his head. He also appeared to vomit into a towel during the difficult stretch.Despite the problem, Djokovic stayed on court and tried to fight his way back into the match. Tirante won the second set 6-4 and then took the third by the same score to complete a 2-6, 6-4, 6-4 victory.Speaking after the match, Djokovic did not blame the conditions alone. He explained that he already has a health problem that becomes harder to manage in hot and humid weather.“It’s because of a health issue I have. I’ve been dealing with it for many years now. It causes me a lot of problems, especially when there’s a lot of humidity and heat,” Djokovic said, according to the ATP Tour.He also explained that the pressure of competing can make things worse.“I did anticipate it [would be humid], but there are all these things, like nerves and everything involved that make it worse, and that’s what happened,” Djokovic said.Djokovic did not name the condition, so there is no confirmed information about exactly what health problem he was referring to. The ATP Tour also reported that he described the match as a difficult physical experience.While Djokovic was dealing with his physical problems, Tirante stayed focused and took advantage of his chances. The 25-year-old Argentine did not let the unusual situation distract him and kept putting pressure on the 24-time Grand Slam champion.After the match, Tirante called the victory the biggest win of his career. He said he handled the pressure of facing Djokovic well and thought about his family and friends back home in Argentina while playing.“I think I really did a good job inside the court. I managed very well the nerves of playing against a legend like Novak,” Tirante said, according to Forbes.Djokovic’s early exit also leaves his future at the Cincinnati Open uncertain. Article Title: Cristiano Ronaldo drops bombshell retirement hint: ‘This is probably my last year’, reveals plans after football
Article Text:

The career Ronaldo is preparing to leave behind

Cristiano Ronaldo has said the 2026-27 season could be the final year of his playing career, offering his clearest indication yet that retirement is approaching. The 41-year-old has spent more than two decades at the highest level and, with his contract at Al Nassr running until June 2027, has now begun speaking openly about what he wants his life to look like once football is over.“This is probably my last year of football, and I want to leave a spectacular legacy,” Ronaldo told Vogue in an interview published on Sunday.Ronaldo has previously spoken about retirement without committing to a particular date. In November, he said he expected to continue playing for “one or two years” and confirmed that the 2026 World Cup would be his final tournament.Portugal were eliminated by Spain in the round of 16 last month. Ronaldo scored three goals at the tournament and became the first player to score at six different World Cups, finishing his World Cup career with 11 goals from 27 appearances.He was less specific about his overall playing future after Portugal's exit. His comments toare the closest he has come to putting a timeframe on it.Ronaldo said he has already planned for the period after football and expects to spend more time with his family, travel and play and watch padel.“I have my future all mapped out,” he said. “I have so many things to keep me busy that to tell you just one thing is hard.“Because football could leave a big hole, you have to fill your time in various ways, not just one. And also have more fun, travel more, watch and play padel, which I really like, and continue to enjoy what I've earned -- what we've earned.“Because after all it's been 25 years with a lot of sacrifice.”Ronaldo remains contracted to Al Nassr until June 2027 and has continued to play for Portugal after the World Cup.He is also 24 senior goals short of reaching 1,000, a milestone he has spoken about wanting to achieve during the latter stages of his career.Portugal's new manager, Jorge Jesus, described Ronaldo as a “symbol of Portuguese football” after taking the job in July and said he would continue selecting him while the forward remains fit and playing.Ronaldo's three goals at the 2026 World Cup took his international total to 146, the highest in men's international football.His club career has continued alongside those international records. He began at Sporting CP before moving to Manchester United, Real Madrid, Juventus and Al Nassr. His most prolific spell came in Madrid, where he scored 450 goals in 438 appearances, becoming the club's all-time leading scorer.Ronaldo has won five Ballon d'Ors and five Champions League titles, along with league championships in England, Spain and Italy. With Portugal, he won the European Championship and Nations League.His career has also produced records across club and international football, including his position as men's international football's leading goalscorer and his six World Cup appearances.The 2026 tournament was already established as the end of his World Cup career. Now, with the new domestic season beginning, Ronaldo has indicated that the wider playing career could have only one more season left.His comments came in an interview conducted five days before his marriage to Georgina Rodríguez in Cascais, Portugal. The couple had been together for nearly a decade before announcing their marriage with a photograph of their wedding rings.Ronaldo has also spoken about wanting to spend more time with his family after football and about the interests he intends to pursue away from the sport.Ronaldo's comments came shortly after Lionel Messi expressed uncertainty over how much longer he would continue playing following the death of his father, Jorge.The pair have spent much of the past two decades at the centre of football's defining individual rivalry, collecting major individual awards and setting scoring records while playing for Barcelona, Real Madrid and their respective national teams.Both are now 39 or older, with Ronaldo at 41 and Messi at 39, and both have recently spoken about circumstances that could bring their playing careers towards an end.For Ronaldo, there is still football to play, goals to chase and a contract that extends into 2027. But for the first time, he has put the possibility of retirement at the end of the current season into his own words.
Article Summary: Cristiano ronaldo says the 2026-27 season could be the final year of his playing career. The 41-year-old has spent more than two decades at the highest level. Ronaldo has previously spoken about retirement without committing to a date. He remains contracted to al nassr until june 2027.

Super Bowl LXI is about to create a very unusual sporting dilemma. The NFL ’s championship game is scheduled for February 14, 2027, putting it on Valentine’s Day for the first time in Super Bowl history. With romance and football competing for the same Sunday, fans have already begun joking about dinner reservations, watch parties and the ultimate relationship compromise.The date alone is enough to make the 2027 Super Bowl stand out. The game will take place at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, on February 14, meaning couples will have to decide how they want to spend one of the biggest nights on the American sporting calendar.For football fans, the answer may seem obvious. For couples with different priorities, however, the evening could require some negotiation.Social media has already embraced the idea. One Reddit commenter joked about the pressure on restaurants, writing:"The Valentine's Day brunch reservations are going to be harder to get than a Super Bowl ticket."Another post took the joke even further, imagining the holiday as a test of romantic loyalty:"Super Bowl on Valentine's? Peak relationship apocalypse incoming—guys choosing touchdowns over touchy-feely dates. Ladies, demand a halftime proposal or it's single season next year."The humor works because the conflict is so easy to imagine. A romantic dinner could overlap with pregame coverage. A reservation might clash with kickoff.And anyone hosting a Super Bowl party could suddenly find themselves planning around Valentine's Day expectations.There is also a convenient escape route. The game falls on Presidents' Day weekend, giving many people the chance to turn the occasion into a longer celebration. Couples could celebrate Valentine's Day on Saturday, watch the Super Bowl on Sunday and use Monday to recover from the late night.The unusual date is not the only reason Super Bowl LXI will be significant. ESPN will broadcast the championship game for the first time in network history, with ABC also carrying the event. ESPN has already outlined extensive programming and storytelling designed to build anticipation well before the game itself.The timing also feeds into a broader conversation about the Super Bowl calendar. The NFL has long faced calls to make the Monday after the championship game a national holiday, particularly because fans already tend to treat Presidents' Day weekend as a natural extension of Super Bowl celebrations.Commissioner Roger Goodell has previously discussed how changes to the NFL schedule could eventually push the Super Bowl toward Presidents' Day weekend. In comments cited in the original report, he said:"I think if you went to 18 weeks regular season that would probably occur," Goodell said at the time. "It is possible somewhere in the calendar. Could happen before that just because of the calendar, the way it lays out.But I think 18 weeks would get you to that point, and I think it would be a really great move."For now, February 14, 2027 remains a one-of-a-kind collision between football and romance. The NFL has confirmed the date, and fans have plenty of time to decide whether Super Bowl Sunday will be a date-night disaster, a couples' tradition or simply the perfect excuse to order wings and watch football together.

Brock Lesnar and Ric Flair are two of the biggest names in professional wrestling. But they have had very different experiences in terms of money. Lesnar was a crossover combat-sports star after excelling in amateur wrestling, WWE and the UFC, while Flair made his name over more than four decades in WCW and WWE.But there is a big gap, and public net-worth numbers are best seen as estimates, not audited financial statements. Lesnar’s contracts in the modern era, UFC purses and limited-appearance model allowed him to make individual paydays that were much larger than what was generally available to wrestlers during Flair’s peak years. Meanwhile, Flair continues to earn from his name, appearances, licensing and wrestling-related projects, despite the financial difficulties that have beset his wealth over the years.Brock Lesnar seems to be in a better financial state at the moment. Celebrity Net Worth estimates his net worth at $10 million, whereas NDTV reported an estimate of $17 million in June 2026. Other outlets have published higher numbers, a testament to the uncertainties that come with calculating celebrity net worth.Ric Flair is worth much less. His net worth has been estimated to be $500,000 by Celebrity Net Worth, but other estimates online have put the figure at a much higher number.The variation reflects the absence of publicly verified personal financial records, and the challenge of calculating assets, liabilities, royalties and ongoing income for a longtime entertainer.Lesnar’s wealth is intrinsically tied to his ability to command top dollar. He was an instant star in WWE after debuting in 2002, but he later moved away from the wrestling world to try his hand at the NFL and mixed martial arts before returning to WWE as an established crossover star.Lesnar’s career in WWE has been as much about scarcity as it has been about star power. He was often employed on a limited schedule around major storylines and premium live events for most of his later career instead of working weekly.Lesnar’s UFC career distinguished his money story from most WWE stars. After leaving professional wrestling, he came into MMA and immediately became a big draw. Beating Randy Couture for the heavyweight championship at UFC 91 made him a legit heavyweight champion and gave him a serious bump in commercial appeal.Lesnar has also earned money from endorsements and appearances. Jimmy John’s and other commercial deals are among his previous endorsement deals, and his celebrity status has helped his value outside the ring.He has also kept his lifestyle very private. Recent reports have pointed out that he prefers a rural lifestyle and owning vast amounts of land, rather than the high-profile celebrity lifestyle that many sports stars enjoy.Ric Flair’s financial story started in an era when the economics of professional wrestling were very different. The Nature Boy became one of the defining stars of the National Wrestling Alliance, World Championship Wrestling and WWE, headlining big events and winning championships through a career that spanned several decades.Flair made a ton of money in his time with WCW. One published estimate puts his WCW earnings from 1996-2000 at about $1.95 million. But the size of his earnings did not translate directly into lasting wealth because of taxes, legal obligations, medical expenses and other financial pressures.He also made a lot of money from his WWE career. Flair was a wrestler, manager and personality and stayed a close associate of the company for years. In 2005, during a divorce hearing, it was revealed that his annual WWE salary was reportedly around $500,000, showing how much he could make from wrestling even later in his career.Of the two stars, Flair's financial history is the starkest contrast. Celebrity Net Worth states that in 2000, the IRS filed a lien of more than $870,000 against him, and his further tax problems damaged his finances. The same source reports that in 2019 there was a major medical emergency that resulted in a medical bill of approximately $1.8 million.These pressures help explain why lifetime earnings and current net worth can look so dramatically different. Making millions in a career doesn’t always translate to keeping millions after taxes, debts, medical expenses and other costs.Lesnar’s future financial prospects will probably continue to be linked to his standing as a top-tier combat sports attraction. As his active wrestling career is changing, his name still has value for special appearances, merchandise, licensing and media projects.Flair’s earning model is a unique one. At 77, his money-making opportunities are increasingly linked to his legacy rather than regular ring competition. He still turns up at wrestling events, signs autographs and does other promotional stuff.Lesnar has a path to victory in the modern economics of sports and one of the rare WWE-to-UFC crossover careers. Flair’s financial legacy isn’t so much the wealth he has today, but the incredible value he brought to pro wrestling in terms of sales. Their careers demonstrate two different paths a wrestling superstar can take to earn money: Lesnar with premium modern contracts and crossover sports earnings, and Flair with longevity, character, championships and lasting brand recognition.

Lesnar was a crossover combat-sports star after excelling in amateur wrestling, wwe and the ufc. Flair made his name over more than four decades in wcw and wwe.

The New Jersey Devils will enter the 2026-27 season without a clear No. 1 goaltender, but Hall-of-Fame goalie Martin Brodeur believes Nico Daws deserves a real chance to take the job. After moving Jacob Markstrom to the Florida Panthers, New Jersey has left the door open for a new starter to emerge.Jake Allen and David Rittich are also in the mix, but Daws could have the biggest opportunity of his young NHL career. Brodeur, who serves as the Devils’ executive vice president of hockey operations, believes the 25-year-old deserves an opportunity to show what he can do in the NHL.According to Brodeur, the Devils are comfortable letting their goaltenders compete for the starting job rather than naming a clear No. 1 before the season begins. “The best starter is going to get the net,” Brodeur told The Hockey News. “I don't think there's a clear-cut No. 1 goalie in net.”That gives Daws a real opening. The 2020 third-round pick has spent much of his career moving between the NHL and AHL, and Brodeur believes the Devils have not given him enough chances to show what he can do.“Nico Daws is a kid who needs a chance,” Brodeur said. “We've been developing him for four years.We didn't put great teams in front of him in Utica and obviously his development slowed down because of that. But we need to give him a chance to see what we have.”While Daws has limited NHL experience, he has already delivered one performance that stands out. In the Stadium Series game against the Philadelphia Flyers at MetLife Stadium, he stopped 51 shots. Brodeur still remembers that performance when discussing Daws’ potential.“We put him into the Stadium Series game at MetLife Stadium in front of 70,000 people and he had 51 saves against the Flyers. He's got it, I really believe in him, we just never gave him a chance,” Brodeur said.That belief could be important for Daws as he competes with Allen and Rittich. Allen brings much more NHL experience, while Rittich has also spent years in the league. But neither has been locked into a heavy workload in recent seasons.Brodeur acknowledged that Markstrom will be missed but believes the current group can give New Jersey what it needs.“Jake showed us a lot last year when he had to play. He played some solid minutes for us,” Brodeur said. “We feel that both goalies are able to play.”If Daws can make the most of his opportunity, he could quickly move from an inexperienced option to the Devils’ top goalie. Inspiring story on motherhood by Naomi Osaka: “Taking care of myself is part of taking care of my daughter”- Tennis star reveals how self-care changed her approach to parenting

What did Naomi Osaka mean when she said self-care is part of motherhood ?

How did becoming a mother change Naomi Osaka’s view of tennis?

Why are boundaries so important to Osaka as a mother?

What can mothers learn from Naomi Osaka’s mental-health journey?

For Naomi Osaka, becoming a mother did not mean putting her own needs aside. Instead, it changed the way she thinks about self-care, mental health and life. The four-time Grand Slam champion, who has been open about her struggles with anxiety and pressure, has shared a simple but powerful message: “Taking care of myself is part of taking care of my daughter. ” Her words show why looking after yourself can also be an important part of being a good mother.Osaka became a mother in July 2023 when she welcomed her daughter, Shai, with rapper Cordae. Her journey into motherhood came during a major change in her life. She had stepped away from tennis for more than a year and was also trying to understand what she wanted from her career and her life.For Osaka, self-care is not about putting herself before her daughter. It is about making sure she is in a good place so she can also be there for her child.In her conversations about motherhood and mental health, Osaka has spoken about setting boundaries, taking time for herself and paying attention to what she needs. That can mean taking a quiet moment, meditating, getting enough rest when possible or simply saying no when something feels like too much.Her message also pushes back against the idea that mothers must always put themselves last.Being a mother does not mean a woman has to ignore her own feelings, needs or identity.Osaka’s approach is simple. A mother can love her child deeply and still need time for herself. In fact, taking care of her own mental and emotional health can help her be more present for her child.Tennis had been a huge part of Osaka’s life for years. She became world No. 1 and won four Grand Slam singles titles, including the US Open in 2018 and the Australian Open in 2019, 2021 and 2022.But success also came with pressure. Osaka made headlines in 2021 when she withdrew from the French Open after explaining that media duties were affecting her mental health. She later stepped away from tennis for an extended period.Becoming a mother gave her another chance to look at her life from a different point of view.Osaka returned to professional tennis in January 2024 after giving birth. The comeback was not easy. She had to rebuild her body, return to the demands of professional sport and deal with the normal ups and downs of competition.But motherhood also helped her understand that tennis was only one part of who she was.Winning was still important to her, but it was no longer the only thing that defined her. She could be a tennis player, a mother and her own person at the same time.That change in thinking also helped Osaka become more open about her emotions. Instead of feeling that she always had to appear strong, she became more comfortable talking about difficult moments and asking for support.Osaka has spent much of her career in the public eye. Her matches, interviews and personal life have all received huge attention. That level of attention can be difficult for anyone, and motherhood has given her even more reason to protect her private life and mental space.She has spoken about how hard it once was for her to say no because she worried about disappointing people. Over time, she learned that she could not make everyone happy and did not have to accept every demand placed on her.That lesson became an important part of how she approaches motherhood.For Osaka, boundaries can mean choosing when to work, taking time away from social media, protecting family time or simply refusing to take on something that could leave her overwhelmed.These choices are not about shutting people out. They are about knowing when she needs to step back.Her experience also sends an important message to other mothers. Saying no does not mean you care less. Taking a break does not mean you are lazy. Asking someone for help does not mean you have failed.Sometimes, protecting your own peace is what allows you to give more of yourself to the people you love.Perhaps the biggest lesson from Osaka’s story is that mental health should not be treated as something people have to hide.She has spoken openly about anxiety, pressure and the challenges that came with being a top athlete. She has also talked about wanting her daughter to grow up in an environment where talking about feelings is normal.Osaka has encouraged the idea that children should be able to express themselves, ask for help and understand their emotions. She has also talked about simple habits such as meditation, quiet time and spending meaningful time with family.For her, these lessons are not only things she can tell her daughter. They are things she can show her through her own actions.When a mother rests when she needs to, she shows her child that rest is important. When she talks about her feelings, she shows that emotions are normal. When she asks for help, she teaches her child that nobody has to deal with everything alone.That may be one of the most important parts of Osaka’s message.Motherhood does not have to mean losing yourself. A woman can still have dreams, a career, friendships, personal goals and time for herself while being a loving and devoted mother.Osaka’s journey shows that self-care is not about choosing yourself instead of your child. It is about making sure you are also cared for.For the tennis star, that balance has become part of the mother she wants to be. Her words, “Taking care of myself is part of taking care of my daughter,” capture that idea in the simplest way. Taking care of yourself is not taking love away from your child. Sometimes, it is what helps you give that love with more patience, energy and presence.
